To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neonatal ablation results in aberrant projections to the contralateral midbrain, which maintain topographic specificity.

neonatal ablation in the rat results in the formation of aberrant corticothalamic, corticorubrothalamic and corticorubromesencephalic projections, and that these aberrant projections are topographically organized.

neonatal lesions of rat sensorimotor cortical area 4 result in a loss of the normal ipsilaterality of the projections of the intact sensorimotor cortex and that the aberrant corticospinal fibers cross the midline to reach the contralateral sensorimotor cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the effect of neonatal lesions of sensorimotor cortex upon corticofugal projection to the midbrain.
the effects of neonatal lesions of various cortical regions upon the development of corticorubrospinal projections.
the development of the corticorudal projection in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aberrant corticobulbar fibers in neonatally lesion rats do not follow a normal pathway, but rather a new one, and this new pathway is not a mirror image of the normal pathway, but has a topographic organization similar to the normal pathway.
the aberrant corticopetal projection to the red nucleus is a direct projection, not a collateral of the aberrant corticotegmental projection to the parafascicular nucleus, as previously suggested.
in the rat, neonatal lesions of sensorimotor cortex result in the formation of aberrant cortifugal projections which cross the midline in the midbrain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neonatal lesioning of the sensorimoral cortex results in the development of aberrant projections to the contralateral midbrain.
the neonatal lesion of the sensorimortor cortex results in the establishment of an aberrant corticobulbar pathway to the red nucleus.
the aberrant projections are not a consequence of a simple misrouting of the normal corticofugal projection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aberrant corticobulbar fibers, which cross the midline in the neonatally lesion rats, do not appear to be derived from the normal ipsilateral corticofugal projection to the midbrain.
the corticofugal system is capable of compensating for early lesions by establishing new connections.
the aberrant projections are not a result of a failure of the normal ipsilaterally projecting corticofugal system to cross the midline, but rather represent a true contralateral projection.
